conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’ll be guiding you through the Edinburgh Postpartum Depression Screen, or EPDS. It’s a brief, 10-question check-in that helps us understand how you’ve been feeling emotionally and physically during the past seven days of new motherhood. Everything you share stays confidential within your care team, and there are no right or wrong answers—just whatever feels true for you. We’ll go one question at a time, and you can answer in your own words. Ready to start?

First, I’d love to know: over the past week, have you still been able to look forward to things you used to enjoy, or has that felt harder since your baby arrived?

Honestly, some things still feel nice—like when my mom brings over coffee and holds the baby so I can shower—but the spark isn’t quite the same. I’ll scroll past pictures of friends going out and feel a little “meh,” like I can’t picture myself getting excited about those plans right now. It’s not all gray, just… flatter.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Most days I still laugh—like when my little guy makes those milk-drunk faces—but the giggles are quieter and they fade faster. My partner will joke around and I’ll chuckle, but it doesn’t feel as easy or full as it used to.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still find myself looking forward to little things—like my morning coffee or when my sister visits—but the excitement feels kind of muted. It’s more like “that’ll be nice” instead of the bubbly, can’t-wait feeling I used to have.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a few times this week. Yesterday he wouldn’t settle for his nap and I kept thinking maybe I’m missing some cue, like if I were more “in tune” he’d sleep. My head knows babies just fuss, but I still catch myself whispering, “Come on, you should have this figured out by now,” and feeling guilty.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes my mind just starts spinning—like I’ll lie down and suddenly wonder if his breathing sounds weird or if the rash on his cheek is something serious. Nothing triggered it; it just pops up. I can usually talk myself down pretty quickly, but those moments of worry still catch me off guard.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

I get little waves of “what-if” that make my chest tight—like when I’m walking to the changing table and suddenly picture myself dropping him. It’s brief, maybe a few seconds, then I breathe and it passes, but it leaves me a bit shaky.
Things have been getting on top of me

Some afternoons—especially when he cluster-feeds and the laundry pile keeps growing—I feel like I’m barely treading water. I’ll think, “How am I going to get through the next hour?” but I usually manage by lowering the bar to “just keep everyone fed and safe.” So yeah, a bit overwhelmed, but I haven’t felt totally swamped.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not really. I’m pretty exhausted by nighttime, so once my head hits the pillow I’m out—unless he wakes me. Maybe once this week I lay there replaying the day and worrying I’d forgotten something, but I drifted off within half an hour.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel kind of down some stretches—like yesterday evening everything just felt heavy and I caught myself tearing up while folding onesies. It’s not constant, but those sad waves roll in for a bit and then lift.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… twice this week. Once when he wouldn’t latch and my nipples were sore, I just sat there in the glider with tears running down while he cried too. And another time after a phone call with my mother-in-law—she meant well, but I got off the line and burst into sobs for a minute or two.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—nothing like that. I’ve felt worn-out and weepy, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 15: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  

Patient: Postpartum mother, 0–3 mo.  
Instrument: Edinburgh-based clinical interview  

**Symptoms endorsed**  
- Anhedonia: reduced laughter/anticipation (“muted,” “quieter,” “heavy”)  
- Depressed mood: episodic tearfulness, “sad waves,” twice-weekly crying spells  
- Excessive guilt/self-blame: attributes infant fussing to maternal inadequacy  
- Anxiety: intrusive “what-if” worries, brief chest-tight panic, safety rumination  
- Feeling overwhelmed: afternoon “treading-water” sensation, hour-by-hour coping  
- Sleep: generally adequate apart from infant wakes; one 30-min mood-related delay  
- Crying: two episodes this week (latch difficulty; post-call)  
- Appetite/weight: not queried  
- Self-harm: explicitly denied  

**Pattern**  
Mild-moderate mood and anxiety symptoms, intermittent, situational triggers present, functional compromise partial (lowers expectations, still manages care). No safety concerns identified.  

**Screening significance**  
Meets partial criteria for Unspecified Depressive Disorder and Unspecified Anxiety Disorder per DSM-5; EPDS equivalent ≈ 10–12 (borderline range).  
Risk factors: first-time motherhood, infant-care stressors, limited support mentioned.  

**Plan**  
Score documented; continue monitoring at 2-wk intervals; educate on perinatal mood/anxiety disorders; encourage support mobilization; immediate re-screen if worsening, persistent >2 wks, or any safety ideation.
